browser.name: Browser
browser.text: Holds only an httpOnly session cookie: never a token, never the API address.

gateway.name: Edge gateway
gateway.text: The one public entry: routes the www, admin and auth hosts.

bff.name: Next.js BFF
bff.text: Server-rendered pages and Server Actions: the only code that calls the API.

keycloak.name: Keycloak
keycloak.text: OpenID Connect sign-in; administrators need a password and an OTP.

redis.name: Redis
redis.text: Tokens sealed on the server and refreshed once, even under concurrent requests.

krakend.name: KrakenD
krakend.text: The private API gateway: verifies every JWT before forwarding.

api.name: NestJS API
api.text: Verifies the JWT again, enforces roles and ownership, writes through Prisma.

postgres.name: PostgreSQL
postgres.text: The data and its outbox, written in one transaction.

nats.name: NATS JetStream
nats.text: Delivers every event from the outbox at least once.

notify.name: Notifications
notify.text: Consumes events through an idempotent inbox: nothing is handled twice.

storage.name: Object storage
storage.text: File bytes go straight between browser and storage with presigned URLs.

nails.name: Envy Nail Spa
nails.summary: From a printed menu and business card to a bilingual salon website with the full price list.
nails.brief: The salon had a beautiful printed menu, a business card and a gift certificate, but nothing a customer could open on a phone. The goal: make every price and service findable in seconds, and make calling or booking one tap away.
features: The complete printed menu as an 8-tab price list, with dotted leaders like the paper version
Seven signature pedicures with “what’s included”, from Basic to Royal Herbal Detox
Gift certificates, salon policy and opening hours in the visitor’s format (12-hour in English)
Brand restyle from the print: forest green, gold foil and the “EN” monogram redrawn in SVG
Mobile drawer menu with scroll-spy, smooth scrolling and a sticky call button
decisions: Facts and prices as typed data, words in per-language dictionaries: a missing translation fails the build
No invented content: reviews, ratings and staff were removed because the business is real
Unreadable menu items are left out and flagged instead of guessed

laundry.name: SFaster Laundry
laundry.summary: A cheerful laundry site with a live price estimator built from the shop’s price board.
laundry.brief: The shop’s strongest selling point (“one customer, one machine”) and its price board only lived on the street sign. Customers needed to know what a load would cost before walking in.
features: Price estimator: pick clothes or bedding, slide the weight, see the price instantly
All four price tables (wash & dry, bedding, dry cleaning, extras) formatted in đồng
How it works, loyalty card (wash 7 times, get 1 free), drop-off tips and FAQ
Visual identity taken from the shop sign: green, yellow lettering, red accents
Zalo and call buttons always within reach on phones
decisions: The estimator is a pure function tested on every tier boundary (3 kg, 6–7 kg gap, 7 kg)
It only computes in the browser: nothing is sent, so no server action or data storage is needed
Phone photos resized with their EXIF rotation applied

wine.name: Khang Hưng Tửu
wine.summary: A heritage brand site in lucky red and imperial yellow, built with alcohol-advertising rules in mind.
wine.brief: A 30-year-old winery with a dense printed brochure and a counterfeit problem: customers had to be told that the only real ordering number is the one printed on the can.
features: Signature product line with photos cut from the brochure, on the exact yellow (#ffe500) of the originals
Showroom jars with the company price per xị, serving guides for steamed wine and Highlands jar wine
Anti-counterfeit notice and the single ordering number repeated where it matters
Restaurant partnership section (display towers and cabinets)
Mandatory 18+, pregnancy and drink-driving warnings next to every call to buy
decisions: No health or medicinal claims, as Vietnamese law requires for alcoholic drinks
Ingredient lists withheld until the owner confirms them: the scans are unreadable in places
Product names kept as printed in every language; everything else translated

wedding.name: Hải Sơn & Trúc Giang
wedding.summary: A wedding invitation website with countdown, lunar date, add-to-calendar and a photo album.
wedding.brief: A paper invitation can’t show photos, a map or a countdown, and guests lose it. This invitation lives at a link: everything a guest needs, in Vietnamese or English.
features: Full-screen hero with a live countdown to the reception
Traditional invitation wording with the lunar date (âm lịch) computed automatically
Ceremony and reception cards with map, Google Calendar and Apple/Outlook (.ics) buttons
Our story timeline and a masonry album with a keyboard-friendly lightbox
Private by link: hidden from search engines
decisions: All dates in Vietnam time whatever the guest’s device says, covered by tests
Lunar date from Intl’s Chinese calendar plus the can chi year name (Bính Ngọ)
The countdown renders placeholders on the server and fills in after hydration: no mismatch on a prerendered page

profile.availability: Open to AI engineering roles & freelance projects
profile.tagline: I build production web systems end to end, from the database to Kubernetes, and take AI agents and RAG from prototype to reliable, secure production.
bio: I’m a senior fullstack engineer with 10+ years building web products, at companies including Lazada, FUTA Bus Lines and OneSecure, and I led a 10-person team at Urbanos. Before that I spent four years as a technical consultant on enterprise security products.

I work across the whole stack: PostgreSQL tuning on million-row tables, NestJS microservices, Next.js frontends, and the Kubernetes, GitOps and monitoring that keep them running. The platform behind this site shows how I build: a private API behind a gateway, tokens verified twice, events delivered through an outbox, CI on every pull request, and every decision written down.

My current focus is AI engineering: agents, RAG and tool calling with LangGraph and LangChain on OpenAI and Azure OpenAI, made secure, observable and cost-aware in production. I’m open to AI or senior fullstack roles, and I build websites and web apps for businesses as a freelancer.

project.name: Microservice platform with BFF websites
project.summary: The repository behind this site, designed and built alone: NestJS microservices behind a private KrakenD gateway, Keycloak identity, PostgreSQL, NATS JetStream events and six Next.js BFF websites, all on Kubernetes with GitOps and telemetry.
points: JWTs verified at the gateway and again in each service (RS256 + JWKS); tokens never reach the browser
Role-based access plus “only the creator or an admin” ownership rules; admin site behind password + OTP
At-least-once events: transactional outbox, JetStream and an idempotent inbox
Optimistic concurrency with ETags, single-flight token refresh, file uploads straight from browser to storage
CI on every pull request, images to GHCR, Argo CD GitOps and Grafana telemetry
24 architecture decision records and written conventions that people and AI coding agents both follow
